subject: Clarify: penetration-test coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC) deployments
messages:
From: Rebecca Moore <security@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2028-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pen test report request + scope question for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our vendor assessment we need the most recent penetration test report and a short summary that clearly states which Redwood environments were included. Specifically: does the report and evidence cover Hosted (shared), Dedicated (reserved fleets), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, or a subset?

Our procurement team requires: 1) an explicit scope matrix, 2) confirmation of whether attacker-origin assumptions include customer-configured private networks, and 3) a remediation status table for any findings. Can you provide the report or a redacted summary for Brightline Health?

Goal: confirm coverage for our SOC2 map and risk register by 2028-04-28.

Thanks,
Rebecca
Rebecca Moore
Head of Security Operations
Brightline Health
Attachment: vendor_evidence_request_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Moore <security@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request + scope question for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private

Hi Rebecca — great question. Short answer: our latest external penetration test (March 2028) covered our Hosted public endpoints and the management/control plane used by Hosted and Dedicated control planes. It did not include customer-managed Private (VPC) networks or fully air-gapped on-prem appliances by design.

I attached a one-page summary and a scope matrix we can share (redacted). For procurement: we can provide a redacted findings summary + remediation status and an engineer-signed statement of attacker model. Private/VPC deployments are treated as out-of-scope for that external test because they rely on customer network isolation; we do, however, offer guidance and a separate contract for on-prem assessment if the customer requests an on-prem pentest under a scoped statement of work.

I'll loop Laura for legal-approved wording and Neha for the technical scope matrix.

Best,
Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pen_test_summary_stub.pdf (summary stub)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Moore <security@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-22T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request + scope question for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private

Hi Rebecca,

Following up with formal language you can use in the vendor security assessment: 

- Covered in March 2028 external penetration assessment: Redwood-hosted public API endpoints, authentication and token issuance flows, and the control-plane interfaces used for Hosted and Dedicated administration.
- Not covered: customer-managed Private (VPC) endpoints, on-prem packaged appliances, and customer-internal networks or integrations that require customer network credentials.

We can provide: the redacted pen-test executive summary, a findings-remediation matrix (status, remediation owners, target date) and an engineer attestation that describes the assumed attacker capabilities. For Private/VPC customers we provide a separate scoped penetration test engagement under an SOW — this would require access and temporary test windows arranged with the customer.

Let me know if you need specific wording for your SOC2 evidence binder — I can drop that in an email.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Moore <security@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-23T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request + scope question for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private

Rebecca — adding technical detail to avoid ambiguity: 

1) Hosted (shared) environment: included. The test exercised public API endpoints, authentication flows, and simulated multi-tenant traffic patterns. No tenant data exfiltration was demonstrated.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): included for the control and management plane only (i.e., provisioning APIs, model routing interfaces). The compute plane where customer models are executed on dedicated GPUs is isolated and not directly reachable from the internet; the pen test did not attempt to physically access customer compute nodes in Dedicated fleets.

3) Private (VPC) and on-prem: out of scope. Customers control network access and can configure private endpoints. If Brightline would like coverage for VPC-hosted endpoints, we can run a scoped test (we'll need a connectivity plan and test window).

Attachment: requested_pen_test_scope_template.xlsx (we filled the requested columns for your convenience).

Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rebecca Moore <security@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request + scope question for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private

Thanks all — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups for our compliance reviewer: 

- Can you confirm whether the Dedicated control-plane coverage includes the customer-specific provisioning API used during tenant onboarding (we just want to confirm tenant creation flows were tested)?
- Please provide the remediation status table as a CSV or spreadsheet with columns: finding_id, severity, status, owner, eta.

If you can drop the CSV and a short statement on your attacker assumptions by EOD 2028-04-26 we'll be able to move the Brightline contract to legal review next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Rebecca
